message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes in the history of the sport. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he played high school basketball at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he gained national attention as a prodigy. He entered the NBA directly from high school and was selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers in the 2003 draft.

James has played for the Cleveland Cavaliers (2003–2010, 2014–2018), the Miami Heat (2010–2014), and the Los Angeles Lakers (2018–present). He has won four NBA championships (2012, 2013, 2016, 2020), earned four NBA Most Valuable Player (MVP) awards (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013), and has been selected to the NBA All‑Star Game 19 times (as of 2023). He is known for his versatility, athleticism, basketball IQ, and leadership on the court.

Beyond basketball, LeBron is also a philanthropist, entrepreneur, and media personality. He founded the LeBron James Family Foundation, which focuses on education initiatives such as the “I Promise” program for at‑risk youth. He has produced and starred in films and television shows, including the 2018 film *Space Jam: A New Legacy* and the 2021 series *The Shop*. He also owns a production company, SpringHill Entertainment, and has invested in various businesses, including a stake in the sports apparel brand Nike.

LeBron James is celebrated not only for his on‑court achievements but also for his influence on culture, social justice advocacy, and business ventures.
